description: Implement investor question 6 - retention section. Create the HTML section, CSS stylesheet, and JS controller for a 4-stage relationship progression (Connection, Trust, Community, Belonging) that continues the user story from the product walkthrough. Reuses existing walkthrough UI components.
steps: Create css/retention.css with styles for the retention section. Use BEM naming with 'retention' block. Reuse existing walkthrough-phone, walkthrough-card, walkthrough-chat, walkthrough-chat__bubble, walkthrough-avatar, walkthrough-tag, walkthrough-trust, walkthrough-community classes from css/product-walkthrough.css. Add only new styles needed for: section-level layout (retention-section, retention--visible), stage containers (retention__stage), stage labels and headings, timeline/progression indicator between stages, bridge/transition at the end. Keep motion minimal (less than product walkthrough). Include reduced-motion media query. Include responsive breakpoints (768px, 1024px). Follow design token usage from variables.css.

Add the HTML section in index.html AFTER the closing </section> of product-walkthrough-section and BEFORE </main>. Section id='retention-section', class='retention-section', aria-label='Why users keep coming back', aria-hidden='true'. Include 4 stages each with [data-reveal]: Stage 1 'Connection' (conversation deepens - show chat history growing with Maya K., deeper topics), Stage 2 'Trust' (verification + shared activities - reuse walkthrough-trust pattern, show growing trust indicators and shared activities count increasing), Stage 3 'Community' (individual to group - reuse walkthrough-community pattern, show Alex bringing Maya to a group, new introductions through trusted connections), Stage 4 'Belonging' (long-term, part of something - show the network grown, multiple communities, Alex now introduces others). End with a bridge div transitioning to the business section. Continue using same characters: Alex (user), Maya K. (MK, indigo), Sam P. (SP, emerald), Jordan L. (JL, amber).

Create js/sections/RetentionSection.js following the exact pattern of ProductWalkthrough.js: export class RetentionSection with constructor (element = getElementById('retention-section')), _setupObserver() using IntersectionObserver with [data-reveal] targets and 'retention__element--revealed' class, _handleIntersections(), reveal(), hide(), isVisible(), destroy(). Use slightly higher threshold for less motion feel (threshold: [0, 0.15, 0.25]). No function >60 lines, no class >400 lines.
Add '@import ./retention.css;' to css/main.css AFTER the product-walkthrough.css import line.

In js/app.js: add 'import { RetentionSection } from ./sections/RetentionSection.js;' after the ProductWalkthrough import. Inside the DOMContentLoaded handler, after productWalkthrough.reveal(), add: const retentionSection = new RetentionSection(); retentionSection.reveal();
Commit all changes with message: feat(product): implement investor question 6 - why users keep coming back
acceptance_criteria: index.html contains section#retention-section after product-walkthrough-section with 4 stages (Connection, Trust, Community, Belonging)
css/retention.css exists with BEM-named styles, responsive breakpoints, reduced-motion query
js/sections/RetentionSection.js exists with reveal()/hide()/destroy() methods and IntersectionObserver
js/app.js imports and instantiates RetentionSection after ProductWalkthrough
No function exceeds 60 lines, no class exceeds 400 lines
Content focuses on relationship continuity, NOT monetization/revenue
Reuses existing walkthrough UI component classes (walkthrough-phone, walkthrough-card, walkthrough-chat, etc.)
Bridge at end transitions to business section
All stages use [data-reveal] attribute for progressive reveal
Section uses aria-label and starts with aria-hidden='true'
verification: Run NODE_OPTIONS='' node -e "const fs=require('fs'); const html=fs.readFileSync('index.html','utf8'); console.log(html.includes('retention-section'));" to confirm section exists
Run NODE_OPTIONS='' node -e "const fs=require('fs'); const css=fs.readFileSync('css/main.css','utf8'); console.log(css.includes('retention.css'));" to confirm CSS import
Run NODE_OPTIONS='' node -e "const fs=require('fs'); const js=fs.readFileSync('js/app.js','utf8'); console.log(js.includes('RetentionSection'));" to confirm JS import

Run NODE_OPTIONS='' node -e "const fs=require('fs'); const code=fs.readFileSync('js/sections/RetentionSection.js','utf8'); const lines=code.split('\n'); const fns=code.match(/\b(reveal|hide|destroy|_setupObserver|_handleIntersections|isVisible|constructor)\s*\(/g); console.log('Methods:', fns.length >= 6 ? 'OK' : 'MISSING');" to confirm all methods exist
findings: All acceptance criteria met. 4 stages (Connection, Trust, Community, Belonging) implemented with progressive reveal. Reused walkthrough-phone, walkthrough-chat, walkthrough-trust, walkthrough-community, walkthrough-avatar components from product-walkthrough.css. RetentionSection.js is 105 lines, all functions under 60 lines. CSS is 351 lines with responsive breakpoints and reduced-motion support. No monetization or revenue content. Bridge transitions to business section.
